venue: NY State Pavilion, Flushing Meadow Park

songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy ’69 set with pedal‑steel Hard To Handle and epic jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show erupts with a jaw‑dropping pedal‑steel take on “Hard To Handle,” solid renditions of “Dire Wolf” and “Dupree’s Diamond Blues,” and a thunderous jam through “Alligator.” Jerry’s guitar work shines, the drums are among the best Dupree’s tracks ever captured.
ai_show_review.review: Recorded at the NY State Pavilion during the 1969 World’s Fair, this performance captures the Dead in top form. The first half crackles with intensity – a rare pedal‑steel “Hard To Handle” that has become legendary, followed by a soulful “Dire Wolf,” a rollicking “Dupree’s Diamond Blues,” and a high‑octane “Alligator” that segues into an expansive “Death Don't Have No Mercy.” The second half keeps the momentum rolling with one of the most praised drum performances on a Dupree’s track and a soaring “The Other One” before closing with “Turn On Your Lovelight.” While the matrix source mixes hissy audience ambience early on, it switches to clean board sound for later numbers, preserving both historic atmosphere and musical clarity. For fans who want crystal‑clear detail, the excellent soundboard of the same night offers a pristine version of “Death Don't Have No Mercy” and vivid stage detail, but the mixed‑source recording remains the most complete document of this iconic set.

best_recording.reason: Captures the rare pedal‑steel Hard To Handle and full show flow; later board sections are clear, making it the most complete historic document despite some hiss.

key_highlights: Pedal‑steel rendition of “Hard To Handle” – a show‑stopping moment
One of the best Dupree’s drum tracks ever recorded
Powerful “Death Don't Have No Mercy” captured on the excellent soundboard
High‑energy jam through “Alligator” and seamless segue into the second set

band_performance.Jerry: Shows off a rare pedal‑steel line on “Hard To Handle,” delivers strong vocals on “Dire Wolf,” and adds memorable guitar solos (notably on the “Sitting On Top Of The World/Big Boss” segment).
band_performance.Phil: Provides solid bass foundation throughout; sings on “Mama Tried,” though his low end is sometimes buried in audience recordings.
band_performance.Bob: Opens with priceless jokes, contributes lead vocals on “Mama Tried,” and adds effective backing vocals across the set.
band_performance.Pigpen: Delivers crunchy, soulful organ work and powerful vocal performances, especially on “Death Don't Have No Mercy” and other Pigpen‑led numbers.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are highlighted as fantastic—one of the best Dupree’s drum tracks ever—with dynamic fills and top‑hat texture throughout the jams.
band_performance.Billy: Partners with Mickey to create a driving, 'crazy' rhythmic backbone; his drumming shines during the extended “Alligator” jam and transitions.
